**The Weight of a Thousand Words**

I sit here, staring at the blank page, the cursor blinking like a metronome counting down the seconds of my indecision. A thousand words—what a strange, arbitrary number. A thousand steps could take you nowhere if you’re walking in circles. A thousand dollars might buy you freedom or just a month’s rent in a city that doesn’t care if you sleep. A thousand words could be a manifesto, a confession, a eulogy, or just the ramblings of a mind too tired to edit itself.

I think about the things that haunt me. Not ghosts, not in the way stories tell them—no sheeted figures floating through walls. My ghosts are quieter. They’re the conversations I didn’t finish, the emails I never sent, the apologies I swallowed because pride is a bitter pill but regret is a slow poison. They’re the version of myself I thought I’d be by now, the one who had it all figured out, who didn’t flinch at their own reflection.

The world is loud. Too loud. We drown in notifications, in opinions, in the hum of machines that were supposed to make life easier but instead just gave us more ways to be lonely. I remember when silence was just silence, not the absence of a podcast or the pause between TikTok videos. Now, stillness feels like failure, like we’re not optimizing, not hustling, not *doing* enough. But what if doing enough is just… being? What if the most radical act is to sit with your own thoughts and not run from them?

I used to write letters I never mailed. Pages and pages of ink-stained confession, folded into envelopes that gathered dust in a drawer. Maybe I thought the act of writing them was enough—like if I put the words somewhere, even hidden, they’d stop echoing in my head. But words have a way of escaping. They seep into dreams, into the way you hold your coffee cup, into the silence between two people who used to have too much to say.

There’s a tree outside my window. I don’t know its name, but it’s been there longer than I’ve been alive. It sways when the wind tells it to, drops its leaves without apology, grows new ones without asking permission. I envy that. The unapologetic existence of things that are not human. The way a river doesn’t wonder if it’s flowing correctly. The way the moon doesn’t care if you call it beautiful.

I’ve spent too much time trying to be *good*—good at my job, a good friend, a good daughter, a good whatever-the-hell-else. But goodness, like happiness, is a moving target. The second you think you’ve grasped it, the definition shifts. Maybe the goal isn’t to be good. Maybe it’s just to be *here*, messy and uncertain and alive.

I think about the people I’ve loved. Some stayed. Some left like thieves in the night, taking pieces of me I didn’t even know were missing until I reached for them and found empty pockets. Love is a strange alchemy—it can turn lead into gold or gold into ash. You never know which until it’s too late.

There’s a quote I can’t place—something about how we’re all just walking each other home. I like that. The idea that none of us really know the way, but we hold hands in the dark anyway. Maybe that’s all we’re supposed to do. Show up. Stumble. Get back up. Repeat.

I don’t know if any of this matters. Maybe these words will disappear into the void, unread, forgotten. Maybe that’s okay. Not everything has to be a masterpiece. Not every thought needs an audience. Sometimes, the act of spilling yourself onto a page is enough. A thousand words, a thousand breaths, a thousand tiny rebellions against the silence.

The cursor still blinks. The tree still sways. And for now, that’s enough.
